html:
The Umayyad Caliphate was the Muslim empire ruled from Damascus by the Umayyad family from 661 to 750. Its founder was Muawiya, who became caliph after the First Fitna when Ali's son Hasan gave up his claim.

Muawiya made the office a family inheritance when he named his son Yazid as heir. That broke from the earlier choice of caliphs by consultation and led directly to the Battle of Karbala in 680, where Ali's other son Husayn was killed.

Under the Umayyads the empire grew from Spain and North Africa to the edge of India. Arabic became the language of government. The dynasty was overthrown by the Abbasids in 750, though one prince escaped to Spain and founded an Umayyad state there. See the Rashidun and Umayyad caliphates.
